description: **Early exit, output writers, signals, and --lint-framework-use.** `throw new ExitNow(code, message)` ends a command from anywhere in its call stack through the exit step: `finally` blocks run, the command exits `code` (1 to 255), and the message is printed as `error: <message>` (under `--json`, the last error diagnostic); `app.call()` rejects with `ExitError`, and MCP `tools/call` answers `exit code <code>: <message>`. `ctx.out(text)` writes the command's answer and is never hidden by `--quiet`; `payloadRenderer:` declares how a payload reads in human mode; `ctx.document()` writes an `ownsStdout` command's document byte-exactly in both modes. `app.run()` catches SIGINT and SIGTERM while the handler runs and aborts `ctx.signal`; when the handler returns, the command exits 130 or 143 with `error: canceled by signal <SIGNAL>`, and a second signal gets the default action. Every app reserves `--lint-framework-use`, which, run alone from the project root, scans the modules reachable from the `package.json` `bin` entries (test files excluded) for process exits, direct stdout and stderr writes, argv access, and environment reads, and exits 1 listing each finding as `<path>:<line>: <rule>: <message>`.

**The `--json` document is `interface_version` 3, stdout is guarded under `--json`, and warnings and errors are prefixed.** The document carries an `output` member after `payload` (the text `ctx.out` wrote plus captured child stdout, `null` when none), and a child run through `spawn` or `run(argv, { stream: true })` under `--json` no longer writes beside it. While a machine-mode handler runs, `process.stdout.write` is replaced: any byte written outside the framework (`console.log`, `process.stdout`) fails the run with exit 1 unless the code is already nonzero, plus the error diagnostic `stdout written outside the framework: <n> bytes: "<excerpt>"`, and `process.exit` ends the run through the exit step with `process exit called outside the framework with code <code>`. In human mode `ctx.warn` prints `warning: <message>` and `ctx.error` prints `error: <message>`.

**effects-bypass no longer loses a handler at a template substitution.** A `${...}` inside a template literal ended the handler's scope for the check, so a direct call after it went unreported, and the template's text was read as code; regular expression literals are now read as literals too.

A child started through `ctx.effects.spawn` that is still running when its handler ends is now killed (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after one second) and fails the run: exit 1 unless the status is already nonzero, plus `error: child process <pid> was still running when the handler ended and was killed: <argv>`. The exit step no longer waits for such a child. Wait on every child you spawn, or end it with the new `Spawned.kill()`; `Spawned.sendSignal(signal)` sends any signal.
`ExitError` carries `payload`: what the command supplied through `ctx.payload` before its early exit, `null` when it supplied nothing.

Under `--json` a spawned child's stdout now reaches the `output` member in the order it arrives, interleaved with `ctx.out` text, instead of all at once when the child exits; a handler that only awaits `ctx.signal` no longer makes Node exit with status 13 before a signal can arrive; and `spawn` no longer hangs in a program run with `node --input-type=module`.
A `check --tag` expression that does not parse is reported as `error: tag expression: ...` (an `error` diagnostic under `--json`) instead of rejecting the run.

`check --ignore-warnings` and `RunChecksOptions.ignoreWarnings` are removed: `check` stays the full report and exits nonzero on warnings, and the new `failing-checks` command (same selection flags) is the run where only error-level failures fail. Every `[checks.<name>]` in checks.toml must now declare `description` (one non-empty line) and `subject` (the options subject file its option belongs in: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, never `manifest`); a checks.toml lacking either is refused at construction with `checks.toml: check "<name>": missing required field "description"` (or `"subject"`), so add both to every declared check. `--dump-schema` publishes them on each check entry.

**Check values, `failing-checks`, and named hooks.** `app.setCheckValueResolver((name) => CheckValue | undefined)` lets an app assign each check a `{ value, source }`: `off` does not run the check (shown as an `OFF` row with its source), `warn` reports its failures as warnings, `error` runs it as registered; a value above the registered severity, outside the three, or without a source is refused. The new `failing-checks` command runs the same selection as `check` and prints only error-level failures, exiting nonzero exactly when one exists. `[hooks.<name>]` tables in checks.toml (`tag = "<expression>"`) name a selection that `check --hook <name>` and `failing-checks --hook <name>` run, and `check --list` shows each check's value and where it came from.

The check commands' `payload_schema` in `--dump-schema` lists `items` before `type`, as Go writes it, so a checks-enabled app's schema dump is byte-identical across the Python, Go, and TypeScript implementations.
